core_obligations: Assume that x lies in IM for an ideal I of A and use flatness of M to write x as a finite sum of products f_i x_i with f_i in I and x_i in M (proof line 5719).
Form the ideal I' generated by the finitely many coefficients f_1 to f_n and note that x already lies in I'M (proof lines 5719-5720).
Apply minimality of the content ideal to the inclusion I' inside I and conclude that the content ideal is finitely generated (proof lines 5720-5721).

difficulty_reason: The lemma concerns the content ideal of an element x of a flat module over an arbitrary ring: whenever the set of ideals I with x in IM has a smallest element, that smallest element is finitely generated (statement lines 5712-5715). The author's proof is short and completely explicit (proof lines 5718-5721): it takes any ideal I with x in IM, writes x as a finite sum of f_i x_i with f_i in I and x_i in M, and observes that the finitely generated ideal (f_1, ..., f_n) already contains x. The point that has to be seen is the direction of the quantifier: it is not enough to exhibit one finitely generated ideal containing x, one must show that the assumed smallest ideal I cannot need more than the finitely many coefficients that occur in a single expression for x. Flatness of M enters only through the existence of such an expression for every ideal I, and the finitely generated ideal produced is contained in I, so it coincides with I by minimality.
